newsitem.title: UK: Castle Tower set to buy BBC transmission business.
newsitem.headline: Castle Tower set to buy BBC transmission business.

text.p: The BBC said on Friday that a consortium led by Castle Tower Corporation (CTC) of the U.S. was the preferred bidder for its Home Service transmission business.
The consortium also includes TeleDiffusion de France, a subsidiary of the France Telecom Group, Candover Investments Plc and Berkshire Partners LLC.

The BBC and the CTC consortium expect to sign a contract for the sale of the business by the end of the month. Proceeds from the sale will be used by the BBC to help finance its move into new digital services.

The BBC said that Merlin Communications International, a management and employment buy-out team from the World Service's Programme Delivery Service, was the preferred bidder for its World Service transmission business. Merlin is backed by financiers led by invesment capital group 3i Plc.
The BBC said a contract for the sale of the World Service business would be signed as soon as practicable. Proceeds from that sale revert to the government.
The government outlined proposals for the sale of the BBC's transmission businesses in November 1995.
"This will be a good deal for the BBC and all concerned," said BBC Deputy Director-General Bob Phillis.

"Further details will be announced on the signing and completion of the contracts. However, I can say that the preferred bidders have fully satisfied all our requirements for both businesses including pension and other employment considerations," he added.
Assets included in the Home Service sale include freeholds and leaseholds in relation to 740 transmitter sites, including equipment, and the benefits of employment contracts with some 500 staff.
The consortium will also be granted a 10-year contract for transmission of BBC analogue television and radio services.
